related_questions.question: What is the new treatment for cervical cancer?

text_blocks.snippet: New treatments for cervical cancer include advancements in immunotherapy, targeted therapies, and radiation techniques, as well as innovative approaches like TIL therapy and combining chemotherapy with chemoradiation. These advancements offer hope for improved outcomes, particularly for advanced or recurrent cases, and are being investigated for earlier-stage disease as well.
snippet_highlighted_words: advancements in immunotherapy, targeted therapies, and radiation techniques, as well as innovative approaches like TIL therapy and combining chemotherapy with chemoradiation

list.title: Pembrolizumab (Keytruda):
list.snippet: This checkpoint inhibitor is used in combination with chemotherapy for persistent, recurrent, or metastatic cervical cancer. It helps the immune system attack cancer cells by blocking a protein that cancer cells use to evade detection.

list.title: Tisotumab vedotin (Tivdak):
list.snippet: This antibody-drug conjugate targets tissue factor on cancer cells and delivers a chemotherapy agent directly to the tumor. It's approved for recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer after chemotherapy.

list.title: TIL therapy:
list.snippet: This approach uses a patient's own tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), which are immune cells found within the tumor, to fight the cancer.

list.title: Other Immunotherapies:
list.snippet: Research is ongoing to explore different combinations of immunotherapy drugs and their effectiveness in various stages of cervical cancer.

list.title: Bevacizumab:
list.snippet: This monoclonal antibody targets the VEGF/VEGFR pathway, which is involved in blood vessel growth in tumors.

list.title: Targeting specific gene mutations:
list.snippet: Scientists are investigating targeted therapies for cervical cancer based on genetic mutations found in cancer cells, such as those in the RET and NTRK genes.

list.title: Volumetric Modulated Arc Therapy (VMAT):
list.snippet: This advanced radiation technique delivers radiation with greater precision, minimizing damage to healthy tissue.

list.title: Combining radiation with other therapies:
list.snippet: Researchers are exploring how to combine radiation with other treatments, like immunotherapy, to treat advanced cervical cancers.

list.title: Chemotherapy before chemoradiation:
list.snippet: The INTERLACE trial showed that giving chemotherapy before chemoradiation can improve survival for some women with locally advanced cervical cancer, according to the American Cancer Society.

list.title: Dual immunotherapy:
list.snippet: Clinical trials are investigating new dual immunotherapy drugs that target two different aspects of the immune system to enhance its ability to fight cancer.

list.title: Prevention through vaccination and screening:
list.snippet: While new treatments are being developed, cervical cancer is still highly treatable when caught early through screening and prevention through HPV vaccination remains crucial.

related_questions.question: What is the implant for cervical cancer?
related_questions.snippet: When brachytherapy is used to treat cervical cancer, the radioactive substance is usually put inside a special hollow applicator. This applicator is called an intracavitary implant because it is placed inside the vagina, or through the vagina and cervix into the uterus, or both.
